title: Form 146 for Foreign Remittances: CA Certificate & Filing Guide
description: Form 146 is a Chartered Accountant (CA) certified document required for specific foreign remittances from India. Its primary purpose is to help determine the .

faq.a: Form 146 is a certificate issued by a Chartered Accountant for certain foreign remittances, primarily to determine the taxability of the payment and the applicable Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) under the Income Tax Act, 1961.

It is typically mandatory for payments made to non-residents that are chargeable to tax in India (e.g., royalty, fees for technical services, interest) or for specific capital account transactions where the bank requires tax clarity.

faq.q: Can I file Form 146 myself without a CA?
faq.a: No, Form 146 requires certification by a Chartered Accountant (CA). The CA's expertise is crucial for assessing the tax implications and ensuring compliance with complex tax laws and DTAA provisions.

faq.q: Does Form 146 apply to all remittances under LRS?
faq.a: Not necessarily. While LRS allows remittances up to USD 250,000, Form 146 is specifically for *taxable* remittances or when the bank requires a CA's certification for complex capital account transactions to ensure tax compliance.

faq.q: What happens if I don't provide Form 146 when required?
faq.a: If Form 146 is required but not provided, your bank might deduct TDS at a higher default rate, or they may refuse to process the remittance until the necessary compliance is met. This can lead to delays and potential over-deduction of tax.

faq.q: Is Form 146 needed for remittances for family maintenance or gifts?
faq.a: Generally, remittances for family maintenance or bona fide gifts to relatives abroad, which are typically covered under LRS and not considered taxable income for the recipient in India, do not require Form 146. However, always confirm with your bank.

Form 146 is typically valid for the specific transaction for which it is issued. If you have multiple distinct remittances, or if the nature of the remittance changes, a new certificate might be required.
